analysis.title: US Rates Watch: Flows & positioning: slower inflows
key_insights: Shorts got a reprieve after last week's selloff as momentum moved back in their favor. The futures positioning proxy still points to a rally in most of the curve, excluding the front end.

Broader US fixed income fund inflows slowed to a trickle as investors pulled out of long-dated UST funds and Agg-style allocation funds during the selloff. IG funds still see strong inflows and MBS funds saw outflows.
Active US fixed income funds are adding small duration shorts, are positioned in steepeners, modestly overweight MBS and modestly underweight credit.

Foreign official custody holdings of USTs fell another $19bn on the week after falling $21bn the week prior, to the lowest level since 2010. BofA reads custodial holdings as a signal of foreign official selling.
Foreign RRP, which would be expected to move inversely to custody holdings, stayed relatively flat.
Some CTAs re-entered short positions after being stopped out, but to a smaller extent than before, due to higher rates vol.

Futures positioning proxy is biased for the curve to twist flatten after last week's selloff. Longs established over the week moved out of the money and shorts moved into the money. Shorts remain the more concentrated position and the likely pain trade if rates rally, but the threshold is higher after recent price action.
CFTC data did not update because of the Veterans Day holiday. CFTC exhibits are as of 3 Nov 2026, with updated data due in next week's report.
Asset managers went long across the curve with some short covering in the long end, though long-end positioning has declined significantly since September.
Bank assets rose in the week ending Nov 4 on growth in cash, UST and agency securities, MBS, and loans and leases. Domestic deposits picked up alongside other borrowing.

10y UST hedged pickup is negative versus 10y JGBs, 20y JGBs, gilts and 10y Canadian government bonds, and slightly positive versus 10y Bunds. Japanese investors see negative pickup in most compared regions.
Japanese investors' holdings of long and medium term foreign bonds fell $3bn on the week. In October, pensions bought $4.9bn of foreign bonds while banks sold $5.3bn.

Primary dealer holdings fell notably at the long end across cash and futures. Dealer participation in auctions remains low, investment fund participation is elevated, and foreign participation has fallen to under 20%.
UST stripping by pension funds was nearly nonexistent in August despite historically elevated yields.

Historically, the futures proxy is a modest contrarian signal for duration (short positioning precedes rallies), fund regression is trend-following, and CTA betas show no strong relationship to future curve or duration moves.

risk_factors: Higher rates vol is limiting how fully CTAs re-enter shorts.
Persistent foreign official selling, signaled by custody holdings at the lowest since 2010.
Fund outflows from long-dated UST funds and Agg-style funds during selloffs.
vol_and_positioning: Futures positioning proxy implies a bias for rates to twist flatten. Shorts are the more concentrated position and the likely pain trade on a rally, but the threshold is higher after the selloff.

CTAs re-entered short positions to a smaller extent than before stop-outs due to higher rates vol. CTA 10y beta rose notably on the week and non-reportable positions point to a recent increase in shorts.
Fund regression and CTAs are neutral on duration while the futures proxy skews short. CTA positioning, fund regression and futures proxy all skew steeper on curve.
Active funds hold small duration shorts, are in steepeners, modestly overweight MBS and neutral IG risk by PCA beta.

tension_points.bull_case: The futures proxy shows net out-of-the-money positioning is short, which historically precedes a rally in rates, and shorts are the more concentrated position.
tension_points.bear_case: After last week's selloff the threshold for a short squeeze is higher, CTAs are re-adding shorts, and funds hold small duration shorts.
